The consideration of sensor needs consisted of leveraging the updated network architecture diagram from Subtask 8.1.0 to understand how demand response signals would be communicated to each type of DER. This exercise provided clear requirements for device solutioning. Specifically, water heater sensors were deemed necessary to achieve measurements required by the M&V plan. This revealed that relays were necessary to integrate the water heater temperature sensors with the ACE IoT controllers. Sensors and control devices that fulfill these requirements were scheduled for Budget Period 3 procurement. Data governance practices during this budget period included data acquisition from project partners through secure channels (SFTP site with password and time-based access), secure data storage in an AWS S3 bucket, and data anonymization for the data request placed on Connected Communities teams by the National Coordinator in May 2025. The implementation of the M&V plan consisted of solidifying a ground-truth list of DERs involved in the project, bulk collection and inspection of data from project partners who have DERs active, and development of a relational database designed to enable efficient calculations of the metrics laid out in Deliverable 13.0.1. The project team is currently storing two years of one-minute resolution BESS/solar data from 600 residential batteries and PV units, OCPP data from 181 EV chargers, 15-minute interval data from over 700 AMI meters, and BESS/solar data from the USU microgrid facility which was the focal point of the Budget Period 2 Go/No-Go decision. As a part of the extract, transform, load (ETL) process employed to manage incoming data, a data quality module was under testing. This module reports on sampling period consistency (highlighting devices with missing data) and compares measured values to device nameplate capacities to detect outliers. Collectively, the accomplishments in Budget Period 2 have laid a strong foundation for continued progress in Budget Period 3. The successful coordination of sensor requirements, secure and scalable data governance practices, and the robust implementation of the M&V assessment plan have positioned the team to seamlessly transition into active data collection and analysis. With Milestone 13.0.1 completed and Deliverable 13.0.1 on track, the project team was poised to enter the next phase equipped with validated infrastructure, aligned control strategies, and a growing repository of high-resolution DER data. These efforts not only fulfill key objectives but had ensured that the team was well-prepared to meet the technical and analytical demands of Budget Period 3. Data collection through AMI, OCPP, and BESS channels continued until project termination; no additional datasets were added thereafter. 7 Conclusion The UDERMS iCommunity project achieved significant progress toward its original objective of demonstrating a utility-managed, grid-interactive community integrating DERs across diverse building types. Through coordinated efforts among PacifiCorp, Utah State University, the University of Utah, Electric Power Engineers, PNNL, OSI, and other partners, the project developed and tested technical architectures, DER control strategies, cybersecurity frameworks, and data management structures foundational to community-scale DER integration.
